{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011CfhNHvRMywm5Q5f57Xb6a","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"`stencil3d` now runs on the GPU with CUDA. On a 512³ grid it's about **105× faster** than the original (375 → ~39,300 million cell updates per second), and its output is bit-for-bit identical: the result hashes, sum, min/max and samples all match the original program.\n\n**Changes** (only the two existing files were edited; the executable name is the same):\n- **`CMakeLists.txt`:** turns on CUDA, compiles `stencil3d.cpp` as CUDA, targets the installed GPU (`native`), defaults to a Release build and links the CUDA runtime. The `-O3 -march=native -Wall -Wextra` flags still go to the host compiler.\n- **`stencil3d.cpp`:**\n  - The grid is initialized directly on the GPU, and only the final grid is copied back, after the timed section.\n  - One kernel per iteration computes the interior and copies the boundary in a single pass. Each thread handles one (x, y) column and walks through a range of z planes, keeping the values above and below in registers.\n  - The timed region includes a final GPU sync, so the time covers the actual computation.\n  - The 7-value sum is added in the same order as the original.\n\n**Why the division was rewritten:** the RTX 3090 is very slow at double-precision maths, and dividing by 7.0 was the bottleneck. I replaced it with an exact integer calculation that rounds the same way as the normal division, so the results don't change. Zeros, very small values, infinity and NaN still use the normal division. I tested it against the hardware's own division on about 2.6×10¹¹ random and edge-case values plus 8.6×10⁹ consecutive inputs, with zero mismatches. That rewrite alone took a 512³ iteration from 5.6 ms to 3.4 ms.\n\n**Correctness checks:** I compared full output against the original build for the default size, 200×150×97, 512³, and edge cases (2³, 1³, 3×1×5 with 0 iterations, 5×4×3, 33×17×70, 130×3×300). All matched, and `-v` validation passes.\n\n**Performance on the 3090:**\n\n| Version | Time per iteration (512³) |\n|---|---|\n| Original CPU code (single thread) | ~353 ms |\n| First GPU version, normal division | 7.8 ms |\n| Final GPU version | ~3.4 ms |\n\nA memory-only test kernel ran at about 2.8 ms per iteration, so the final version is within about 20% of the GPU's memory-speed limit.\n\n**Things to know:**\n- **Default size:** the default 128³ × 10 run now finishes in under 1 ms. The program measures time in whole milliseconds, so it prints `0 ms` and `inf` performance. That is the original timing code, which I left as is; use bigger grids or more iterations to benchmark.\n- **One GPU only:** the program uses a single GPU even though this machine has four 3090s. Splitting the grid across GPUs could add throughput on large grids, but it needs halo exchanges between GPUs each iteration, so I didn't do it.\n- **Build output:** I removed my `build/` directory, so `stencil3d/` contains only the two original files."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":432,"cache_read_input_tokens":45981,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":432},"output_tokens":3,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"8e02d0ec-7c6e-4199-a3c0-b9d5f65ed91e","uuid":"b8cf414d-41ed-48d9-86b7-76d14659b961","timestamp":"2026-10-04T14:38:35.627Z","request_id":"req_011CfhNHuZXPxPkYV2rdjzZH"}
